structured_output.hypothesis: If Darwin is right, nearly every oceanic island country or territory has at least one native bat (order Chiroptera) species, and many remote ones have bat species found nowhere else.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Take a fixed list of at least 30 oceanic island units, fixed before the data are inspected. (A) The share of these units with at least one extant Chiroptera species in countryDistribution is ≥ 90%. (B) Among units with bats, the share that have at least one bat species whose countryDistribution is that unit alone (single-unit endemic) is ≥ 40%. The claim passes only if both A and B hold.
structured_output.fail_criterion: The claim fails if (A) is below 75%, or if (B) is below 20%. Results between these bounds on either measure are reported as inconclusive and do not confirm the claim.
structured_output.interpretation: "Ærial mammals" means bats (Chiroptera). "Oceanic islands" means islands never joined to a continent. In practice, these are sovereign island states and island territories listed in the MDD countryDistribution field, such as Fiji, Samoa, Tonga, Vanuatu, Solomon Islands, Palau, Cabo Verde, Comoros, Seychelles, Mauritius, Sao Tome and Principe, New Caledonia and Cook Islands. Continental-shelf islands are excluded (Britain, Borneo, Sri Lanka, Taiwan, Japan's main islands). "Almost every" is read as ≥90%. "Endemic" is read as a species whose recorded distribution is a single island unit. Limits: the country level is coarse, so single-island endemics inside an archipelago count as endemic only if the whole archipelago is one unit. Species introduced by people and extinct species are excluded. The chosen units must be listed before analysis. Darwin's contrast with terrestrial mammals is not tested here, because he stated it as background. Only the bat claim is tested.

dataset.name: Mammal Diversity Database (MDD)
dataset.publisher: American Society of Mammalogists (hosted on Zenodo)
dataset.why_it_fits: The CSV file MDD_v*_species.csv lists every recognised mammal species. Fields used: order (filter to CHIROPTERA), sciName, extinct (exclude extinct species), domestic, countryDistribution (to assign species to island units and to find species confined to one unit), and biogeographicRealm. Counting bat species per island unit and single-unit endemics gives measures A and B. The record is CC BY 4.0 and each release has downloadable files. The DOI above is the concept DOI and always resolves to the latest version. I did not confirm that the CSV has an island-level field, so the analysis uses countryDistribution only.
